A paren in a context-changing position -- before `=` or `x`, after
my/our/local/state, after `\` -- makes a list, so perl builds different ops
with it than without. These are the context-changing dropped parens of
perl.git t/, reduced, with one snippet per position the corpus does not
reach. TestDroppedParenPositionsAreClassified (parenpos_test.go) holds psc's
lowering of each to perl's list; this file holds perl's marker counts and
the re-emission.

=== before = : a subscripted scalar in parens (op/taint.t:66)
my (%old, %env, $x);
($old{$x}) = $env{$x} =~ /^(.*)$/;
--- facts
match 1 exact
faithful
# aassign; without the paren, sassign

=== before = : an lvalue call in parens (op/try.t:195)
my @array;
sub flist :lvalue { @array }
(flist) = (4, 5, 6);
--- facts
faithful
# A zero-argument call keeps its source pair before an operator tighter
# than a list operator (issue 01a1692f), so canon writes `(flist) = ...`.

=== before = : the empty list
sub f { (1, 2) }
my $n = () = f();
--- facts
faithful

=== before x : a reference in parens (op/inccode.t:298)
sub fake_module { }
my @inc = (\&fake_module) x 2;
--- facts
srefgen 1 exact
faithful
# repeat lK/DOLIST; without the paren, repeat sK/2

=== after my : a declared list repeated
my @r = (my ($x) x 2);
--- facts
faithful
# Deparse,-p: (my(@r) = ((my($x)) x 2)); repeat lKP/DOLIST over padsv sPM/LVINTRO

=== after my : two declared names repeated
my @r = (my ($x, $y) x 2);
--- facts
faithful

=== after my : a foreach reference alias (op/for-many.t:474)
use feature qw(refaliasing declared_refs);
no warnings;
my @ret;
foreach my (\@array) (["A"], ["B"]) { push @ret, "<@array>" }
--- facts
faithful

=== after our : a declared package list repeated
our @r = (our ($x) x 2);
--- facts
faithful

=== after local : a list assignment
our $x;
local ($x) = 1;
--- facts
faithful
# aassign; `local ($x) x 2` is perl's "Can't modify repeat (x) in local"

=== after state : a state list repeated
use feature 'state';
my @r = (state ($x) x 2);
--- facts
faithful
# Deparse,-p: (my(@r) = ((state $x) x 2))

=== after \ : a parenthesised my, assigned (op/aassign.t:163)
use feature 'refaliasing';
no warnings;
our $pkg10;
\(my $lex) = \$pkg10;
--- facts
srefgen 1 exact
faithful
# aassign; `\my $lex = \$pkg10` is refassign

=== after \ : a parenthesised call (op/sub_lval.t:10)
sub a :lvalue { my $a = 34; ${\(bless \$a)} }
--- facts
srefgen 2 exact
faithful

=== before x : a split in parens (op/repeat.t:62)
my @r = (split(//, "123")) x 2;
--- facts
faithful
# repeat lK/DOLIST; without the paren, repeat sK/2

=== before = : an ampersand call in parens (op/coreamp.t:674)
sub mykeys :lvalue { my $x } my %h; (&mykeys(\%h)) = 1025;
--- facts
srefgen 1 exact
faithful
# aassign; without the paren, sassign

=== a list slice of a call
my $s = (stat "TEST")[7];
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list concatenated
my ($x) . 'a';
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list assigned from another
my ($x) = my ($y) = 1;
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list assigned in a return
sub f { 1 } sub g { return my ($x) = f() }
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list assigned, then a comma
my ($x, $y) = (1, 2), 3;
--- facts
faithful

=== an our list assigned a repeat, then or
our ($x, $y) = (1) x 2 or die;
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list repeated on the right of +
my $y = 1 + my ($x) x 2;
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list repeat-assigned
my ($x) x= 2;
--- facts
faithful

=== a declared list assigned a defined-or
my ($x) = <STDIN> // 0;
--- facts
readline 1 exact
faithful

=== a parenthesised reference list assigned
use feature 'refaliasing'; no warnings; our ($x,$y,$a,$b); \($x, $y) = (\$a, \$b);
--- facts
srefgen 2 exact
faithful

=== a declared list on the right of a tighter operator
my $y = 2 * my ($x) + 1;
--- facts
faithful
# (my($y) = ((2 * my $x) + 1)); fixed by 01a16602-608d's declaration
# operand, which also closes 01a16a7a-a6f4.

=== a declared scalar on the right of a tighter operator
my $y = 2 * my $x + 1;
--- facts
faithful
# (my($y) = ((2 * my $x) + 1));
